fields.features_heading: What Your Lead Routing App Handles
fields.features_subheading: Every new lead passes through your rules in order and leaves with one owner and a record of why.
fields.feature_1:
Rules checked in the order you set

You write each rule as a sentence. The app checks them top to bottom and stops at the first match, and any lead that matches no rule goes to a fallback queue you name.
fields.feature_2:
A rotation that respects caps and time off

Reps take new leads in turn. Set a daily cap for each rep and mark anyone who is away, and the app passes over them until they are back under the cap or back at work.
fields.feature_3:
Existing accounts stay with their owner

The app reads your CRM through its API and matches each lead's email domain to an account. A match goes to that account's owner, whose name is written back to the CRM.
fields.feature_4:
Timers on the first call or email

Each assignment starts a clock. If no call or email is logged before it runs out, the app moves the lead to the next rep and alerts the sales manager in Slack or by email.
fields.feature_5:
A log of why each lead went where it did

Each lead keeps the rule it matched, the rep it reached, and every handoff after that, in a database you own. A rep who asks why a lead skipped them gets the answer there.
fields.feature_6:
The routing app's code in GitHub

Export the full code of the app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Your team can read every routing rule in the code and change it like the rest of your stack.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Rules That Decide Who Gets the Lead
fields.tab_content_1:
A rep with 6 new leads today is skipped in the rotation

Thistlegate Analytics rotates demo requests among 4 reps, each capped at 6 new leads a day. Tobias Wrenfield already has 6 today, so the request from Ines Calloway at Orchard Lane Clinics skips him. It goes to Mireille Okafor, the next rep in line, as a direct message.
fields.tab_content_2:
Leads from a known domain reach that account's owner

A dispatcher at Harrowgate Freight, Wilhelmina Dacosta, starts a trial of Calderwood Fleet Software. Her email domain matches an account Benedikt Sorell already owns in HubSpot. The app sends the lead to him instead of the rotation and adds her as a contact on that account.
fields.tab_content_3:
An untouched lead moves on after 15 minutes

Pellbrook Payroll assigns Annika Lindqvist's quote request to Dorian Hale at 2:05 pm. At 2:20 pm, with no call or email logged in 15 minutes, the app moves the request to Keziah Brandt. The sales manager, Ottavio Renn, gets a direct message saying the lead has moved.
fields.tab_content_4:
Leads written in Spanish go to a bilingual rep

Valentina Arroyo writes her request in Spanish on the contact form at Saltmarsh Learning, an online tutoring company. The app sends Spanish requests to the 2 bilingual reps in turn. It is Rafael Quintero's turn, so he gets the lead, with Spanish marked as her language on the record.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan lead routing automation and its rules, then build it with Emergent and test it on last week's leads.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Decide who is in each rotation
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every place a lead can arrive, such as the demo form, trial signups, or the chat widget. Note the fields each one captures, since a rule can only check a field the lead carries.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put the rules in the order they should be checked, with the narrowest first: account owners, then language, then the rotation. Name the person who works the fallback queue.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List the reps in each rotation and the daily cap for each one. Pick the one place reps mark themselves away, such as a status field in the CRM.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose how many minutes a rep has to call or email a new lead, and who gets the lead next if they do not. Decide what the clock does outside business hours.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the routing in a prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write the rules, caps, and timer in plain English, the way you would brief a new sales ops hire. Emergent builds the routing app from that prompt, with the lead record and the routing log.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect your CRM and your forms through their APIs. Leads then arrive with their fields filled in and ready for the first rule.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Take last week's leads and run them through the app. Compare each owner the app picks with the rep who took the lead by hand, then fix any rule that sent one to the wrong place.

faq_plan.a: Lead routing automation is software that gives every incoming lead an owner on the sales team by rules, as soon as the lead arrives. The rules check fields on the lead, such as company or language, and fall back to a rotation when nothing matches. It takes the place of a person reading a shared inbox and forwarding each request by hand.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up lead routing automation?
faq_plan.a: Write your routing rules as sentences first, in the order they should run, with a fallback for leads that match none. Then describe them in a prompt in Emergent's AI automation builder. Emergent builds the routing app with its lead database and routing log, and you change any rule later by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: What should lead routing automation software check before it assigns a lead?
faq_plan.a: It should check whether the lead already belongs to someone. Look for an open lead with the same email, and an account with the same email domain, before any rotation runs. Then check the fields your rules depend on, such as language or product, and send a lead with an empty required field to the fallback queue instead of guessing.

faq_plan.q: Do lead routing automation tools work inside the CRM or alongside it?
faq_plan.a: A routing app built with Emergent works alongside the CRM: it reads leads through the CRM's API and writes each owner back. Keep routing inside the CRM when every rule uses CRM fields, and pick a separate app when your rules need data the CRM does not hold, such as rep calendars. If you also want follow-up tasks or deal stage changes, that is crm automation, not routing.

faq_plan.q: What should lead routing automation do with a lead that matches no rule?
faq_plan.a: It should send that lead to one named person, never to nobody. Have that person assign it by hand and note why no rule caught it. Read those notes every week, and when the same reason shows up 3 times, write a rule for it and put it in the right place in the order.

faq_plan.q: When should lead routing automation use round robin instead of fixed owners?
faq_plan.a: Use round robin when any rep can handle any lead. Use fixed owners when the relationship matters more than speed, such as an existing customer or a named target account. Combine the two by checking ownership first and sending only unowned leads to the rotation. Emergent builds either setup from a prompt and changes it when you prompt again.

faq_plan.q: Can lead routing automation route leads by the page they came from?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the page travels with the lead: capture it in a hidden form field and write a rule on that field. Group pages by topic, such as pricing pages for senior reps. If your seo automation publishes new pages every week, route by URL path: a new page under the pricing path then lands in the right group with no rule change.

faq_plan.q: What first-touch window should I set in lead routing automation?
faq_plan.a: Set a window your team can meet on its busiest day, such as 15 minutes in business hours, and put a timer on it. A window the team misses every afternoon teaches everyone to ignore the alerts. Decide separately what happens after hours: pause the clock until morning, or send the lead to whoever is on call. In an app Emergent builds, the alert can go out by Slack or email.

faq_plan.q: What should lead routing automation do when a rep leaves the team?
faq_plan.a: It should move that rep's open leads to other reps the same day. Take the rep out of every rotation first, then move their named accounts to the new owner as one batch. Keep the old owner's name on the routing log, which the app stores in a database you own. The history of each lead then still shows who worked it.

faq_plan.q: Where does lead routing automation end and the rest of the sales process begin?
faq_plan.a: Routing ends when the lead has an owner and that owner has made first contact. What comes after, such as follow-up emails and pipeline updates, belongs to sales automation. Keep the two apart: when a routing rule also sends emails, a lead that reaches the wrong rep is much harder to trace.

plan.angle: The top results define lead routing and list routing methods, but none shows the rules firing on a real lead. This page treats routing as an ordered set of rules and shows four of them running for four sellers: a round robin that skips a rep at the daily cap, a known company's lead going to its account owner, a 15-minute first-touch timer that moves an untouched lead, and Spanish-language requests going to the 2 bilingual reps. Scoring, nurturing and the wider CRM stay with their own pages.
